tagline: Two miles of the Fairhaven Turnpike to a 1934 arch.
intro: From the roundabout where Route 79 meets Route 80 in North Madison, the scenic road runs two miles east on Route 80 to the Hammonasset River and the Killingworth line.

It follows the Fairhaven Turnpike of 1824, which came east from the Fair Haven section of New Haven to Killingworth center. Killingworth was named for Kenilworth in England, the old home of the settler Edward Griswold, and over the years the two spellings drifted apart.

moments.title: North Madison
moments.text: Route 79, the Durham Road up from Madison center, meets Route 80 at a roundabout in the village and goes on north toward Killingworth and Durham.

moments.title: Hammonasset River Bridge
moments.text: At the Killingworth line the road crosses the Hammonasset on Bridge No. 1132, an open-spandrel arch the state highway department built in 1934.
